questions.question: What makes Ansible 'agentless'?
options: It connects to managed hosts over SSH and needs no daemon installed on them
It runs entirely in the cloud
questions.explanation: Unlike Puppet/Chef agents, Ansible pushes small module programs over SSH (WinRM for Windows) and executes them; targets need only Python. Nothing to install, patch, or keep enrolled.

questions.question: What does idempotency mean for a playbook?
options: It runs faster on the second execution
Re-running it on an already-converged host makes no changes (changed=0)
It can only run once per host
questions.explanation: Modules assert desired state ('nginx present', 'line exists') rather than performing actions blindly, so repeated runs are safe. That property is what makes scheduled convergence runs and drift repair possible.

questions.question: In a playbook, what does `become: true` do?
options: Escalates privileges (typically sudo) for the tasks
questions.explanation: become switches to a privileged user (root by default, configurable via become_user) — needed for package installs, service management, and writing system paths.

questions.question: When does a handler run?
options: Only when notified by a task that reported CHANGED, and then once at the end of the play
questions.explanation: Handlers are deduplicated, change-triggered tasks: ten config tasks can notify 'reload nginx' and it reloads once, and only if something actually changed — no pointless service bounces.

questions.question: Why prefer the apt/yum/service modules over shell commands like `shell: apt install -y nginx`?
options: Modules are idempotent, report changed-state accurately, support check mode, and are cross-platform-aware
Modules run locally instead of remotely
questions.explanation: shell always reports 'changed', breaks --check, and hides errors in string parsing. Modules know how to test state first. Rule of thumb: shell/command is a last resort, guarded with creates:/when:.

questions.question: Which variable source has the HIGHEST precedence?
questions.explanation: Extra vars (-e) always win; role defaults always lose. In between (simplified): group_vars < host_vars < play vars. Design roles with overridable defaults and inject environment-specifics higher up.

questions.question: Ansible Vault lets you keep encrypted secrets committed in Git and decrypt them at playbook runtime.
questions.explanation: True. vault-encrypted files are ciphertext in the repo; --ask-vault-pass or --vault-password-file (held by CI) decrypts in memory at run time. Rotate the vault password like any credential.

questions.question: `--check` mode guarantees that no task can modify a managed host.
questions.explanation: False in the strict sense: shell/command tasks (and modules without check support) either skip or — if forced with check_mode: false — still execute. Check mode is a strong safety net, not an absolute guarantee; keep raw commands out of playbooks.

questions.question: You must patch 40 web servers with zero total downtime. Which playbook feature is designed for this?
options: forks: 40 to hit all hosts at once
serial: (e.g., serial: 2) to roll through hosts in small batches, optionally with max_fail_percentage
questions.explanation: serial turns a play into a rolling update: 2 hosts leave the pool, patch, return healthy, next batch. Combined with a health-check task and max_fail_percentage, a bad patch stops after the first batch instead of taking down the fleet.

questions.question: Your EC2 fleet autoscales; hardcoded inventory files are permanently stale. What's the Ansible-native fix?
options: A cron job that rewrites inventory.ini hourly
A dynamic inventory plugin (e.g., aws_ec2) that queries the cloud API and groups hosts by tags at run time
questions.explanation: Dynamic inventory resolves hosts live from the source of truth (cloud APIs); tag Name/Role/Env become groups automatically. New autoscaled instances are targetable seconds after boot.

questions.question: Write the ad-hoc command to ping all hosts in inventory.ini.
questions.explanation: Ad-hoc form: ansible <host-pattern> -i <inventory> -m <module>. The ping module verifies SSH + Python on each target (it's not an ICMP ping).

questions.question: Write the command to run site.yml against inventory.ini in dry-run mode showing diffs.
questions.explanation: --check simulates the run; --diff prints before/after for files and templates. The pair is the standard pre-flight before touching production.

questions.question: What is an Ansible role?
options: A conventional directory structure (tasks, handlers, defaults, templates…) packaging reusable automation
questions.explanation: Roles are Ansible's reuse unit: a self-contained bundle applied with a single line in a play. Teams compose plays from roles (base, nginx, app) instead of monolithic task lists.

questions.question: What are 'facts' in Ansible?
options: Per-host system information auto-gathered at play start (OS, IPs, memory), usable in templates and conditionals
The output of the debug module
questions.explanation: The setup module collects facts like ansible_facts.os_family, letting one playbook branch per platform (`when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'Debian'`). Disable with gather_facts: false when speed matters and facts don't.
